incident-bot: [INCIDENT] High 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (hosted) — paging oncall @Riley. 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC

pagerduty-bot: Paging Riley (oncall) — severity: P1, 60% of requests failing for some customers. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-12345 :rotating_light:

Riley: Ack'd. I'm investigating. Any immediate mitigation? Can we fail open to a cheaper compatible model while we debug? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Alex: On it with Riley. I'm running curl against the api gateway now. Sending logs shortly.

Alex: ```
# curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-request-id: 01H8Z... 
error: upstream timeout
``` 

Sanjay: Seeing increased connection resets from runtime pool to model shard 4 (g2.2xlarge). Possibly kernel OOM around the same window. I'm pulling kernel logs.

Maria: Heads-up — one large customer (acme-inc) reported timeouts and has an open support ticket. Customer impact unknown yet. Please triage for SLA exposure.

Riley: Mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic for non-critical tenants to fallback model variant (v1-small) 2) restart affected runtime nodes 3) collect traces for 02:00–02:18 UTC. I'm executing step 1 now.

Sanjay: Step 1 done — traffic routing rule applied. Error rate dropped from ~60% -> ~8% within 90s. Proceeding with node restarts.

Alex: Restarted 3/4 nodes in the pool, one failed to come back (node-7). Captured crash log:

```
Mar 12 02:12:17 node-7 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 21432 (python) score 892 or sacrifice child
Mar 12 02:12:18 node-7 systemd[1]: Started Redwood runtime agent.
```

Riley: Node-7 replaced with new instance; pool healthy. Error rates at ~2% overall. Good. Next: quick post-incident go/no-go for customer comms. Maria, do you want a proactive note to Acme?

Maria: Yes please — they saw retries. I'll draft a short message once we have a concise impact summary. Also need to know impacted tenants and window.

Riley: Timeline for RCA doc scheduling: propose 2026-03-13 15:00 UTC for a 45m postmortem review (async write-up before then). Who can draft the initial RCA? @Sanjay volunteered to draft.

Sanjay: I'll take the first pass. Draft outline will include: timeline, contributing factors (OOM + routing config), customer impact, mitigating actions, and long-term fixes.

Alex: I'll help assemble logs and add the exact request IDs for ACME. Also volunteer to do peer review.

Riley: Action items captured — I'll file them in the incident tracker and assign owners. Quick list (will add Jira links after):
- Sanjay: Draft RCA (due 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC) — initial
- Alex: Collect traces and attach logs (due 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC)
- Maria: Draft customer comms (due 2026-03-13 10:00 UTC)
- Riley: Schedule postmortem meeting and create doc (done)
- Jamie: Sign-off reviewer after peer review (target 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC)

Alex: Template suggestion for RCA — include a short impact summary at top (one paragraph), then timeline, root cause hypothesis, evidence, action items (short + long-term), and risk acceptance if any. Example timeline snippet below.

Sanjay: Draft timeline (WIP):
```
02:10 UTC - anomaly detected by monitors
02:12 UTC - error spike, pagerduty triggered
02:15 UTC - oncall ack and initial mitigation (route non-critical tenants)
02:17 UTC - error rate drops ~90%
02:18 UTC - node-7 OOM observed
02:25 UTC - node-7 replaced
02:30 UTC - all services healthy
``` 

Maria: For customer notes we should include: affected window (02:10–02:30 UTC), symptoms (timeouts/502), remediation steps we took, and next steps (RCA + timeline + follow-up). Tone: apologetic, technical enough for SRE on customer side.

Riley: Peer reviewers: Alex, Maria. Reviewer checklist: 1) verify timeline against traces; 2) confirm customer impact table; 3) sanity-check proposed long-term fixes (esp. autoscaler config and OOM mitigation).

Alex: I'll verify traces and the per-tenant impact. Quick question: do we have autoscaler history for the pool? Could be relevant to OOM.

Sanjay: Autoscaler logs attached to the draft doc (link placeholder). Preliminary cause: a mis-sized memory limit on new model shard causing a memory leak under certain prompt patterns + an aggressive autoscaler that recycled capacity too slowly, compounding OOM risk.

Jamie: Thanks all. I'll be available for sign-off after peer reviews. Please flag the doc with "ready for sign-off" and ping me. Deadline sounds reasonable. :thumbsup:

Riley: Agreed. Next immediate steps: Sanjay will drop draft into the doc (link: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/INC-12345) by 09:00 UTC tomorrow, Alex and Maria will review by 13:00 UTC, Jamie will sign off by 16:00 UTC. Maria will send customer comms after final approval.

incident-bot: ACTIONS CREATED — INC-12345: RCA draft (Sanjay), logs collection (Alex), customer note (Maria), sign-off (Jamie).

Maria: I'll post a short customer note draft in the doc and loop in support for sending once we have sign-off.

Riley: Great work triaging. Leaving this thread open for updates and the draft link. Once sign-off complete, we'll close the ticket and add remediation EPIC to roadmap. :white_check_mark:
